events.text: A proctor sets the question before you in {ct_hall}: "The northern horsemen raid the border every autumn and are gone before the garrisons can march. Propose a remedy." The candle in your cell is half burned already.

choices.text: Write a poem on the border winter (Poetry)
Lay out a plan of forts, scouts and granaries (Strategy)
Copy the old memorial on the border in flawless script (Calligraphy)
Reason from the classics on ruling by virtue (Mind)

events.text: The second paper in {ct_hall} is a map: a walled city, a river, an army twice its size on the far bank. "You hold the city. Write how you would hold it through one winter."

choices.text: Write an ode to the defenders on the wall (Poetry)
Plan the defence: the river, the gates, the rice (Strategy)
Answer in characters so fine the examiners stop to look (Calligraphy)
Argue from the histories which sieges were lost and why (Mind)

events.text: The examiners in {ct_hall} want a poem, eight lines, on a single word written at the top of the paper: "Return". Around you a hundred brushes scratch at once.

choices.text: Write the poem, and let it be about someone who does not come home (Poetry)
Turn "return" into a lesson on retreating armies (Strategy)
Write eight plain lines in perfect running script (Calligraphy)
Write on return in the sense the classics use it (Mind)

events.text: A question in {ct_hall}: "Compose a rhapsody on the plum blossom that opens in the snow, and say what it teaches an official." The cell is cold enough that the ink thickens.

choices.text: Write the rhapsody, snow and blossom and all (Poetry)
Make the plum a general who holds out in winter (Strategy)
Write a short piece and spend the hour on the brushwork (Calligraphy)
Answer with the sages on constancy in hard times (Mind)

events.text: In {ct_hall} you are handed a draft memorial to the throne, clumsy and blotted, and told to "set it in a form fit for the Son of Heaven to read". Every stroke will be judged.

choices.text: Recast it as polished verse (Poetry)
Reorder its arguments so the strongest comes first (Strategy)
Copy it out in the regular script of the old masters, without a single fault (Calligraphy)
Correct its reasoning and its quotations (Mind)

events.text: An examiner in {ct_hall} unrolls an old landscape scroll with no inscription. "Write the inscription this painting deserves, on the painting itself." Your hand must not shake.

choices.text: Compose a poem for the mountains in the scroll (Poetry)
Read the scroll as a map and write about its passes (Strategy)
Write the inscription so it sits in the painting like a bird on a branch (Calligraphy)
Name the painter's school and the sage it follows (Mind)

events.text: The question in {ct_hall}: "The Yellow River has broken its banks in three counties. The granaries hold enough for half the people. What should the magistrate do first, and why?"

choices.text: Write a lament for the flooded counties (Poetry)
Plan the relief: boats, dikes and rationing (Strategy)
Write a short answer in faultless script (Calligraphy)
Reason it through: who first, what first, and the duty of an official (Mind)

events.text: A passage of the classics is printed at the top of your paper in {ct_hall}, with three characters missing. "Supply them, and explain the passage." The candidate beside you is already sweating.

choices.text: Fill the gap with your own verse (Poetry)
Explain it as a teaching on command (Strategy)
Fill the gap in the hand of the original copyist (Calligraphy)
Supply the characters from memory and explain the passage (Mind)

events.text: Three days after the list is read, a minister's steward comes to your lodging with a red card and a very formal bow. The minister's family has a child of marriageable age, and would be honoured to be joined to the house of the Top Scholar.

choices.text: Accept the match with thanks
Decline politely: your heart is your own

events.text: A scuffle in the street outside the office, a falling beam, and without thinking you catch it with one hand. When you look up, a censor is staring at you, and so is half the street. By evening there is a summons on your desk: the pact of non-interference forbids the murim the service of the throne.

choices.text: Accept dismissal and leave in disgrace
Laugh it off: anyone can be strong

fail.log: Nobody believes it, least of all the censor.

choices.text: Go to the quiet man in black who has been waiting in the corridor

events.text: The great court assembles at dawn. The river has flooded the southern provinces, and the treasury can pay for relief or for the new summer palace, not both. The emperor looks down the hall and waits.

choices.text: Speak for relief: the people before the palace
Say the throne will know best how to balance both
Agree with the Inner Court: the palace, and relief from the provinces themselves
Keep your head down and say nothing

events.text: A rider has come from the frontier: the horse tribes have crossed the wall at two passes. The generals want an army; the Inner Court wants a treaty and gifts. Every minister in the hall must speak.

choices.text: Speak for the border villages: defend them, whatever it costs
Ask the emperor's will and promise to carry it out
Side with the Inner Court: silk is cheaper than soldiers
Say nothing, and let the generals and the eunuchs argue

events.text: A censor rises before the court and names a provincial governor: grain stolen from the relief stores, sold at three times the price. The governor is a friend of the Inner Court. All eyes turn to the ministers.

choices.text: Demand a full inquiry and the governor's seal
Ask that the emperor alone decide the matter
Speak for the governor: a misunderstanding, surely
Study the floor tiles until the moment passes

events.text: The chief eunuch proposes that the Inner Court take over the salt monopoly "to spare the ministries the burden". The Pure Stream scholars go pale. The emperor seems to like the idea.

choices.text: Oppose it: the salt belongs to the realm, not the palace
Say that whatever pleases the throne pleases you
Support it, and ask for a small share of the inspection posts
Say nothing at all

events.text: A bad harvest and a full treasury: the Pure Stream asks the emperor to cut the land tax for a year. The Inner Court says the treasury must be kept for emergencies, and for the palace kitchens.

choices.text: Speak for the farmers: cut the tax
Propose a cut where the harvest failed, and full taxes elsewhere, as the throne prefers
Side with the Inner Court: keep the treasury full
Keep silent

events.text: A comet hangs over the capital for a week, and the astronomers say heaven is displeased. The court must advise the emperor: an amnesty, a great sacrifice, or a purge of whoever displeased heaven.

choices.text: Advise an amnesty and lighter punishments
Advise the great sacrifice, led by the emperor in person
Agree with the Inner Court that someone must be blamed
Let the astronomers do the talking

events.text: Your steward arrives at a gallop, without his hat. The people of {ct_fief} have shut the town gates, opened the granary to everyone, and nailed your tax notices to the gate upside down. They say they will not pay another grain this year.

choices.text: Ride out with your guards and break the revolt
Go to the square alone and hear their grievances
Flee to the capital and let the court deal with it

events.text: Torches on the road to your residence. The villages of {ct_fief} have risen together behind a schoolteacher with a loud voice, and they are coming to ask, very loudly, where the taxes went.

choices.text: Bar the gates and send the guards out to scatter them
Open the gates, and invite the schoolteacher in to talk
Leave by the back gate before they arrive

events.text: Dust on the horizon, then banners: a neighbouring lord has marched an army to the walls of {ct_fief}, with a letter claiming the land was his grandfather's. The herald waits at the gate for your answer.

choices.text: Hold the walls
Pay him to go home
Yield the fief rather than see it burned

events.text: A great bandit host has come down from the hills, three thousand strong, and camped in the fields of {ct_fief}. Their chief sends a polite note: the fief, or a ransom, by the new moon.

choices.text: Man the walls and wait for them
Pay the ransom
Give up the fief and lead your people out

events.text: The steppe is flat to the edge of the world, and {ct_foe} come over it at a trot, thousands of riders under horsetail banners. {ct_unit} must be in formation before they arrive. Your scouts report the enemy drawing up in {ct_scouted}. (Wedge beats Fish Scale, Fish Scale beats Crane Wing, Crane Wing beats Long Snake, Long Snake beats Wedge.)

choices.text: Form Crane Wing: wings wide to fold around them
Form Fish Scale: shields locked, a dense centre
Form Long Snake: a long column that bends and strikes
Form Wedge: one hard point to drive through

events.text: The campaign against {ct_foe} comes to a river crossing at dawn. Mist on the water; drums on the far bank. {ct_unit} waits for the order to form up. Your scouts report the enemy drawing up in {ct_scouted}. (Wedge beats Fish Scale, Fish Scale beats Crane Wing, Crane Wing beats Long Snake, Long Snake beats Wedge.)

choices.text: Form Crane Wing: wings wide to fold around them
Form Fish Scale: shields locked, a dense centre
Form Long Snake: a long column that bends and strikes
Form Wedge: one hard point to drive through

events.text: A mountain pass, narrow and long, and {ct_foe} hold the far end of it. The wind carries their drums down to {ct_unit}. There is room for only one formation, and it must be the right one. Your scouts report the enemy drawing up in {ct_scouted}. (Wedge beats Fish Scale, Fish Scale beats Crane Wing, Crane Wing beats Long Snake, Long Snake beats Wedge.)

choices.text: Form Crane Wing: wings wide to fold around them
Form Fish Scale: shields locked, a dense centre
Form Long Snake: a long column that bends and strikes
Form Wedge: one hard point to drive through

events.text: A wide plain of stubble fields, a ruined watchtower, and the army of {ct_foe} drawn up in the morning light. {ct_unit} takes its place in the line. Your scouts report the enemy drawing up in {ct_scouted}. (Wedge beats Fish Scale, Fish Scale beats Crane Wing, Crane Wing beats Long Snake, Long Snake beats Wedge.)

choices.text: Form Crane Wing: wings wide to fold around them
Form Fish Scale: shields locked, a dense centre
Form Long Snake: a long column that bends and strikes
Form Wedge: one hard point to drive through

events.text: Salt wind and wet sand: {ct_foe} have come ashore and formed up on the beach with their backs to the boats. {ct_unit} comes over the dunes. Your scouts report the enemy drawing up in {ct_scouted}. (Wedge beats Fish Scale, Fish Scale beats Crane Wing, Crane Wing beats Long Snake, Long Snake beats Wedge.)

choices.text: Form Crane Wing: wings wide to fold around them
Form Fish Scale: shields locked, a dense centre
Form Long Snake: a long column that bends and strikes
Form Wedge: one hard point to drive through

events.text: The imperial army marches into the mountains of {ct_foe}. Masked fighters in black hold the slopes above the road, and somewhere above them their halls wait. {ct_unit} must form up on broken ground. Your scouts report the enemy drawing up in {ct_scouted}. (Wedge beats Fish Scale, Fish Scale beats Crane Wing, Crane Wing beats Long Snake, Long Snake beats Wedge.)

choices.text: Form Crane Wing: wings wide to fold around them
Form Fish Scale: shields locked, a dense centre
Form Long Snake: a long column that bends and strikes
Form Wedge: one hard point to drive through

events.text: Your spymaster lays a bundle of letters before you, tied with black thread: {ct_plotter} has been writing to the garrison commanders of the capital, and the letters are not about the weather.

choices.text: Have {ct_plotter} arrested tonight
Call {ct_plotter} in and forgive them to their face
Purge every officer who might be part of it
Let the plot run, and watch

events.text: A taster falls ill at the spring banquet, and the cup was meant for you. The trail of the poison leads, by three servants and a cook, to the household of {ct_plotter}.

choices.text: Arrest {ct_plotter} before the banquet ends
Say nothing of it, and send {ct_plotter} a gift instead
Order a purge of the palace and the great offices
Double the tasters and watch who flinches

events.text: At the third watch a palace guard captain asks to see you alone. A gate will be left open tomorrow night, and {ct_plotter} has paid for it. He has brought the silver to prove it.

choices.text: Close the trap: arrest {ct_plotter} at the open gate
Send the silver back to {ct_plotter} with a note: "I know"
Purge the guard and the offices from top to bottom
Leave the gate open, and wait behind it

events.text: Late at night in the office, a ledger does not add up. Someone has been taking rice from the county granary a sack at a time, and the handwriting in the margin belongs to your superior.

choices.text: Report it up the chain

effects.log: The report goes up; your superior goes down. Some colleagues stop talking when you enter.

choices.text: Correct the ledger quietly and say nothing

effects.log: The ledger balances. Your superior finds a small purse on your desk the next morning.

events.text: Rain for nine days in the camp. The rice is wet, the tents are wet, and the soldiers of {ct_unit} are starting to talk about going home without orders.

choices.text: Share your own rations and sit with them by the fire

effects.log: Nobody deserts. Years later some of them still tell the story of the rainy camp.

choices.text: Double the watch and make an example of the loudest

effects.log: The talk stops. So does the singing.

events.text: An old farmer of {ct_fief} walks two days to your residence to ask you to judge a quarrel over a well. Half the village has followed to watch.

choices.text: Judge it fairly, in the courtyard, in front of everyone

effects.log: The village walks home arguing about your verdict, which is a good sign.

choices.text: Send them to your steward

effects.log: The steward settles it. Nobody remembers who the lord was that day.

events.text: A black tablet under your door at night, with a name and an address. The imperial guard has a task for the cultivator who hides at court.

choices.text: Go at once, masked

effects.log: By dawn the task is done and no one saw your face. The court will never know whom to thank.

choices.text: Send the tablet back unopened this time

effects.log: The tablet does not come back for a long while.
